questions.stem: A postoperative client can bear weight but is mildly unsteady when first walking to the bathroom. Which nursing approach provides the safest hands-on assistance during ambulation?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a properly fitted gait belt and walk beside the client, maintaining a secure grasp safely while allowing the client to participate in the movement.","B":"Wrap a folded bedsheet around the client's waist and use it as a transfer handle because improvised fabric provides support equivalent to a gait belt.","C":"Hold the client under both arms during walking because axillary support gives the nurse better control if the client's knees suddenly begin to buckle.","D":"Ask the client to hold onto the nurse's neck or shoulders because direct upper-body contact provides the most stable support during an unexpected loss of balance."}}
questions.rationale: A gait belt can provide a secure handhold for a client who can participate in standing and walking but needs hands-on assistance. It should be properly fitted and used according to mobility assessment and facility policy. Pulling under the arms or having the client hang from staff creates injury risk.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Fundamentals: Transfers and Ambulation
questions.source_detail: Safe ambulation uses an appropriate transfer/gait belt when indicated and avoids unsafe improvised or axillary pulling techniques.

questions.stem: A client recovering from shoulder surgery can move the affected arm through part of the prescribed range but needs assistance to complete the motion. Which exercise description is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Passive range of motion means the client contracts the muscles independently while the nurse observes the joint without assisting or guiding the movement.","B":"Active range of motion means the nurse moves the joint through the prescribed arc while the client remains relaxed and contributes no muscle effort.","C":"Active-assisted range of motion means the client initiates the movement and receives help to complete the prescribed range that cannot yet be reached alone.","D":"Resistive range of motion means the joint is moved without muscle contraction so mobility can be maintained while the affected extremity remains completely relaxed."}}
questions.rationale: Active ROM is performed by the client; passive ROM is performed for a client who cannot move the joint independently. Active-assisted ROM is appropriate when the client can initiate movement but lacks sufficient strength or mobility to complete the prescribed range alone.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf — Nursing Fundamentals: Range of Motion
questions.source_detail: Active-assisted ROM combines the client's voluntary movement with assistance to complete the available prescribed range.

questions.stem: A client with a new colostomy reports repeated pouch leakage and burning of the skin directly around the stoma. Which teaching best addresses the likely cause while protecting peristomal skin?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Apply an oily moisturizing cream under the skin barrier at each change because a lubricated surface improves adhesive contact and prevents effluent from reaching the skin.","B":"Re-measure the stoma and fit the barrier opening closely around its base, changing the system promptly when leakage or burning occurs rather than reinforcing the leak.","C":"Cut the barrier opening noticeably larger than the stoma so pressure is avoided, even if a rim of peristomal skin remains exposed to stool beneath the pouching system.","D":"Keep a leaking pouch in place until the routine change day because frequent replacement damages skin more than continued exposure to stool beneath a loosened barrier."}}
questions.rationale: Leakage allows stool to contact peristomal skin and is a common cause of irritation. WOCN guidance recommends a barrier opening that fits closely around the stoma base and prompt pouch-system change when leakage, burning, or itching occurs; simply reinforcing a leak or leaving exposed skin under an oversized opening can worsen injury.
questions.source_name: WOCN — Peristomal Skin Assessment Guide for Consumers
questions.source_detail: WOCN advises routinely measuring the stoma, sizing the barrier opening closely around the stoma base, and changing the system promptly for leakage, burning, or itching.

questions.stem: An older adult removes complete dentures for nighttime care. Which instruction best protects the dentures while also supporting effective cleaning and storage?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Brush the dentures with a stiff brush and abrasive whitening toothpaste, then leave them completely dry overnight so the acrylic surface can fully air out safely.","B":"Rinse the dentures with very hot water before storage because high temperatures disinfect the appliance without changing its shape or surface properties.","C":"Store the dentures dry in an uncovered cup and clean them only when visible debris appears because daily soaking can weaken properly fitted denture material over time.","D":"Clean the dentures with an appropriate nonabrasive method, avoid hot or boiling water, and keep them in water or denture solution when they are not being worn."}}
questions.rationale: Dentures should be cleaned regularly with a method that does not damage the material. ADA guidance warns against hot or boiling water because it can warp dentures and recommends keeping dentures in water or an appropriate solution when not worn so they do not dry out.
questions.source_name: American Dental Association — Denture Care and Maintenance
questions.source_detail: ADA guidance supports daily nonabrasive cleaning, avoiding hot or boiling water, and keeping dentures moist in water or denture solution when not worn.

questions.stem: A client with no history of skin cancer asks which daily habits provide the most effective general protection from ultraviolet exposure. Which teaching is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use sunscreen mainly on clear summer days because cloud cover blocks most clinically important ultraviolet exposure and protective clothing adds little benefit.","B":"Use broad-spectrum, water-resistant SPF 30 or higher on exposed skin, seek shade, wear sun-protective clothing, and reapply sunscreen as directed when outdoors.","C":"Use indoor tanning instead of outdoor tanning because artificial ultraviolet exposure produces cosmetic pigmentation without meaningfully increasing skin-cancer risk.","D":"Skip sunscreen on darker skin tones because naturally higher melanin prevents clinically important ultraviolet injury and makes other sun-protection measures unnecessary."}}
questions.rationale: AAD recommends a layered sun-protection strategy: seek shade, wear protective clothing, and apply broad-spectrum, water-resistant SPF 30 or higher to exposed skin, with reapplication as directed. UV exposure occurs on cloudy days and affects people of all skin tones; tanning beds also expose users to carcinogenic UV radiation.
questions.source_name: American Academy of Dermatology — Skin Cancer Prevention
questions.source_detail: AAD recommends broad-spectrum, water-resistant SPF 30+ sunscreen, shade, protective clothing, and reapplication approximately every 2 hours or after swimming/sweating.
